page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m1.xlarge is an x86_64 instance configuration featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs distributed across 2 physical Intel Xeon cores running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. Hyper-threading allocates two threads per physical core, supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of shared L3 cache. System memory is sized at 4.0 GB, yielding a 1:1 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 1.0 GB per vCPU. The server does not bundle local disk storage and contains no discrete graphics accelerators, requiring attached cloud storage for operating system and data requirements. Baseline network bandwidth is provisioned at 2 Gbps.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate moderate single-threaded capability alongside constrained multi-core scalability. The instance attained a Geekbench single-core score of 1345.0 and a single-core stress-ng result of 1783.99, placing it within typical mid-tier boundaries for its clock speed. Instruction set support includes AVX and AVX-512F alongside cryptographic AES instructions. In multi-threaded testing, performance is constrained by the two physical core threshold, showing a Geekbench multi-core score of 2944.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 5283.73. Memory throughput reflects 28.55 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 23.42 GB/sec for writes.

With a lean memory allotment of 1.0 GB per thread, the ecs.u1-c1m1.xlarge prioritizes compute thread availability over memory-intensive footprinting. This hardware configuration offers an economical deployment target for workloads where memory capacity is not the bottleneck. The instance fits stateless web serving, reverse proxying, worker queue consumption, build pipelines, and distributed utility services with minimal cache requirements.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m1.xlarge is an x86_64 virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical Intel Xeon cores clocked at 2.5 GHz, paired with 4.0 GB of RAM. The instance lacks local disk storage and GPU hardware, relying on external network-attached storage and offering a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Supporting AVX-512F and AES instructions, the platform achieves mid-tier single-threaded benchmark output, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1345.0 and stress-ng single-core rating of 1783.99. Multi-threaded performance is bounded by its dual physical core structure, recording a Geekbench multi-core mark of 2944.0. The 1:1 ratio between vCPUs and gigabytes of system memory creates a compute-skewed density profile that trades memory buffer space for execution threads. Consequently, the instance functions effectively for stateless application runtimes, lightweight web proxies, asynchronous task processors, and low-footprint microservices.
